news_list.title: Revival 0.3.0
news_list.short_description: A new balance for casual play with presets, monsters where the wiki puts them, summoning scrolls and charms, fairer experience, and many fixes.
news_list.content:
What changed in 0.3.0:

FIXED
- Oils give their bonus against their monsters again, and so do the oil skills (Enhanced Oils, Superior Oils, Fixative, Protective Coating). They took effect before the fight had a target, so they did nothing.
- Resolve, Precise Blows, Crushing Blows and Razor Focus work, and so do Ursine Armor, Hermit's Armor and the Wolven swords. They need the critical hit meter, which did not exist yet when they took effect.
- Blizzard fills a quarter of the critical hit meter when the fight starts, as its description says.
- Hit Reflection works: a perfect parry reflects 30% of the damage back (it reflected nothing).
- The Melltith sword's fire damage works: every hit has its 15% chance.
- Nemeta: finishing one with no bomb equipped no longer leaves the game waiting for the server.
- Each nemeton stays at the same spot every day. Its monsters still change daily.
- Lothar's map costs 500 orens when you buy it (it was free). If you already have it, you keep it.
- Bestiary: monsters you fought but did not beat stay after the server restarts, and a won fight counts even if the monster's time on the map ran out during it.
- Your chosen head stays after a restart (it went back to the first one).
- Real weather works on the phone. Before, the server could not reach the weather service, so the weather was always clear. After a failed look (no network) it tries again within a minute.
- The game starts without an internet connection. Its clock now comes from the phone, like the server's.
- The Google sign-in window no longer pops up in the game, and the settings no longer have the account section (sign-in, user id, log out). It only linked accounts on the original servers.
- The sea is on the map. OpenStreetMap has no sea areas, only coastlines, and the map now draws the sea from them.
- After a new map (built again, another region, or one built after you first played) the game drew the old map tiles it had kept. It now drops them when the map changes.
- Dashboard: choosing a preset sticks (it went back to Custom), and on the phone its questions show (the name of a copy, confirmations). Saving changes to Revival or Vanilla on the phone did nothing before.
- The Rewards page fits a phone: each row is a card, and long item lists wrap.
- A legendary summoning scroll summons a legendary at any level. Below level 10 it gave a common monster.
- The Experience and Ingredients Scrolls and the charms show their own icons among the effects on the map, and the trinkets' attack bonuses show a sword. They were white squares.

REBALANCED FOR CASUAL PLAY
The companion's dashboard now has presets on its Tuning page: Revival (this balance, the default), Vanilla (the original game) and your own. Everything below that differs from the original game can be switched or changed there.
- Quests pay more: about twice the experience, two to four times the orens, and items that suit their monsters (oils, potions, bombs, summoning scrolls, Experience and Ingredients Scrolls). The Great Mushrooming also gives an extra set of saddlebags (+400 slots).
- Daily tasks pay twice their gold, plus 200 experience and an item (a potion, oil, bomb, summoning scroll, bait or booster).
- Nemeta pay 100 orens and twice the experience.
- Level-ups also give 100 orens (250 every fifth level) and a summoning scroll every fifth level, with the original game's potions, oils and bombs.
- The inventory starts at 400 slots (was 200) and can grow to 2000. Every bag stays in the shop.
- Bestiary tiers need fewer kills: common 3/25/100, rare 2/10/20, legendary 1/2/4.
- Quest places stay within 800 m of you when the map allows, and never farther than 1 km.
- Trinkets give bonuses, written in their descriptions: more herbs, experience and attack against a family, more ingredients, more orens from nemeta, bag slots, and a second crafting station for the season journal.
- No packs of orens in the shop, and the game no longer offers to sell you orens when you are short.

NEW
- Summoning scrolls lure the monsters you want: five of a family (draconids, necrophages, specters...), three commons, a rare or legendary elemental or ogroid, or a legendary. The shop sells them beside the baits.
- Experience Scroll (+100% experience for 30 minutes) and Ingredients Scroll (+50% ingredients from fights and herbs).
- Charms for rain, fog or clear skies where you are, for an hour (250 orens). Rain brings out the monsters that like it, and the Squall potion works.
- The dashboard's Rewards page: what each quest ending pays (experience, orens, items, slots), the daily task items and the level-up rewards.
- Open your herbalist's packs yourself: in the inventory, a pack's button reads Open, and each pack gives 5 bundles of herbs. You can still send them to friends, and you are on your own friends list too: send a pack to yourself and open it there.
- Several map areas at once: if you play across a border, add the region next door. Update or delete your areas in the companion app (guided setup, Map areas). Your map so far is your first area.
- Dashboard debug tools: give yourself a trinket (or take it back) to try its bonus.
- Everything this update adds to the game is in all of the game's languages, and so are these notes.

MONSTERS AND EXPERIENCE
- Where and when monsters appear follows the Witcher wiki's Monster Slayer bestiary, and the game's bestiary says so. Monsters of all natural environments keep off streets (parks in towns are fine), rain brings water monsters inland, increased activity makes a monster more likely at its time, and you meet monsters for your level: one skull from level 3, two from level 6, legendaries from level 10.
- Eight monsters have the wiki's rarity: Tiger Fiend, Leecher, Pale Fleder, Green Forktail, Writher and Sea Witch are common, Grimnir and Royal Foglet rare.
- A fight pays experience by rarity (common 100, rare 250, legendary 600), as the original game did; it went by a hidden difficulty before. The new-monster bonus knows the monsters you met in the story.
- A fight still pays if the server restarted during it, a repeated reply no longer pays nothing, a lost level-up window comes again, and the game shows the experience the server saved.

GOOD TO KNOW
- This update changes the game itself: tap Update the game in the companion app.
- Settings you saved before are kept as the preset Custom. Choose Revival on the Tuning page for the new balance.
- The original game's level table is a switch on the Tuning page. Your level stays the same when you switch.
- For the sea, build your map again in the companion app. Maps built before 0.3.0 have no coastline.
- On the coast, the waterline and piers no longer hold places for monsters, as with lakes and rivers.

Weather data by Open-Meteo.com. Map data from OpenStreetMap contributors. Questions and reports: join our Discord from the companion app.
